title: Vardhan Silicon Works gets board approval for 300 mm mixed-signal fab in Gujarat
body: Vardhan Silicon Works has received board approval to build a 300 mm mixed-signal fab at its Gujarat campus, with an estimated investment of INR 18,000 crore over five years. The first phase targets 20,000 wafer starts a month at 40 nm and 65 nm nodes for automotive and industrial power management chips. The company said it will begin placing orders for lithography, deposition and process control metrology tools in the first half of 2027 and has set up a dedicated tool procurement office. The company has shortlisted a site with access to ultra-pure water and a dedicated power line, and said it is in talks with automotive customers about long-term capacity reservation agreements.

title: Kaveri Assembly & Test adds second OSAT line for power modules
body: Kaveri Assembly & Test will add a second outsourced semiconductor assembly and test line at its Mysuru facility, dedicated to power modules and discrete packages for electric vehicles and solar inverters. The capacity expansion adds 1.2 million units a month and is backed by a long-term customer agreement with an EV powertrain maker. Kaveri said it is sourcing die attach, wire bonding and automated optical inspection equipment and expects the line to qualify by September 2027. The company's existing line runs close to full utilisation, and it said demand for power module packaging from EV and renewable energy customers has doubled over the last eighteen months.

title: Voltrix Motors to design its own traction inverter, seeks silicon carbide power IC partners
body: Voltrix Motors will bring traction inverter design in-house for its next generation of electric SUVs, due in 2028, and has opened a power electronics design centre in Pune. The company said the move will improve range and reduce dependence on imported inverters. Voltrix is seeking long-term supply partners for silicon carbide MOSFETs, gate drivers and battery management ICs and plans to finalise at least two semiconductor suppliers before the end of this financial year. The company sold about 52,000 electric vehicles last year and expects in-house power electronics to lower the cost of its drivetrain by close to 15 per cent over the life of the platform.

title: Meghdoot Electronics commits INR 1,400 crore to new EMS plant for automotive electronics
body: Meghdoot Electronics will invest INR 1,400 crore in a new electronics manufacturing services plant in Sriperumbudur, focused on automotive control units, chargers and battery management systems. The new plant will run 14 SMT lines at full capacity and start production in the second half of 2027. Meghdoot said component localisation is a priority, and it is qualifying Indian and Asian suppliers of power ICs, microcontrollers and sensors for its automotive programmes. Meghdoot currently supplies consumer electronics and industrial customers, and said automotive contracts already signed will account for about a third of the new plant's first-year output.

title: Tejasvi Semiconductor announces INR 9,500 crore compound semiconductor fab in Odisha
body: Tejasvi Semiconductor has announced a INR 9,500 crore compound semiconductor fab near Bhubaneswar that will make silicon carbide and gallium nitride power devices. The fab has received state incentive approval and is applying for central support. Tejasvi said construction of the cleanroom starts in January and that it has begun discussions with vendors of epitaxy, wafer inspection and film thickness metrology tools, with first tool move-in planned for early 2028. The company has signed a technology licence with an overseas partner for its first device generation, and it said it expects defence, railway and EV customers to take most of the initial output.

title: Nexora Packaging raises Series B to build advanced packaging OSAT in Hyderabad
body: Nexora Packaging has raised USD 65 million in a Series B round to build an advanced packaging and test facility in Hyderabad for flip-chip and system-in-package products. The OSAT will serve fabless companies designing chips for telecom, consumer electronics and automotive markets. Nexora said the first production line will be installed by mid-2027 and that it is evaluating wafer-level inspection, X-ray metrology and final test handlers from several suppliers. Nexora was founded by former packaging engineers from global OSAT companies, and said several fabless customers have already committed to qualifying products at the new Hyderabad facility.

title: Silvane Microsystems opens 600-engineer analog design centre in Bengaluru
body: Silvane Microsystems, a fabless analog chip company based in Singapore, has opened a design centre in Bengaluru that will employ 600 engineers by 2028. The centre will develop power management ICs and battery monitoring chips for two-wheeler and passenger EV customers. Silvane said it will tape out its first products at partner foundries next year and is building a local characterisation and reliability lab that will need test equipment and wafer probers. The company said India is now its fastest-growing market, and it expects the Bengaluru team to own the full product cycle from specification to production testing for several product lines.

title: Surajpath Power Electronics to build 8 GW solar inverter plant in Chakan
body: Surajpath Power Electronics will build an 8 GW solar string and central inverter plant in Chakan to serve rising demand from rooftop and utility-scale solar projects. The INR 750 crore project is due to begin production in mid-2027. Surajpath said the plant will need large volumes of IGBT modules, silicon carbide diodes and gate driver ICs, and it wants to sign multi-year supply agreements with semiconductor makers that can support local inventory. Surajpath currently makes about 2 GW of inverters a year, and said strong demand from rooftop solar programmes and utility tenders has left its existing lines booked out for the next nine months.

title: Lehar Telecom Equipment launches 5G radio unit manufacturing in Noida
body: Lehar Telecom Equipment has launched manufacturing of 5G radio units at a new plant in Noida with a capacity of 150,000 units a year. The company won an order to supply radios to a national operator's network roll-out. Lehar said the radios use RF front-end chips, power amplifiers and power management ICs that are currently imported, and it is working with chip suppliers to secure supply and local technical support. The company expects to add a second production line next year for small cells and private network equipment, and has hired 150 engineers for design and testing at the Noida site.

title: Krishna Consumer Devices starts laptop assembly with 1 million unit annual capacity
body: Krishna Consumer Devices has started laptop and tablet assembly at its new Greater Noida plant with an annual capacity of 1 million units under a contract manufacturing deal with two global brands. The investment of INR 600 crore also includes a motherboard SMT line. The company said it plans to add a power adapter and charger line next year and is qualifying suppliers for power ICs, USB-C controllers and battery chargers. The state government has approved incentives under its electronics policy, and Krishna said its brand partners want local suppliers for chargers and power accessories within two years.

title: Raftaar Electric raises funding to double electric scooter output and build BMS in-house
body: Raftaar Electric has raised INR 400 crore to double production of its electric scooters to 30,000 units a month and bring battery management system design in-house. The company plans to set up a battery pack line at its Hosur plant next year. Raftaar said the in-house BMS will use cell monitoring ICs, isolated gate drivers and microcontrollers, and it is looking for semiconductor partners with automotive-grade parts and application engineering support in India. Raftaar sold about 160,000 scooters last year and said recent battery safety rules have made in-house control over battery management design a priority for the entire product range.

title: CloudKey Data Centres orders custom power shelves for 40 MW AI campus in Navi Mumbai
body: CloudKey Data Centres is building a 40 MW AI-ready data centre campus in Navi Mumbai and has asked local electronics makers to design custom 48V power shelves and rack power distribution units for high-density GPU clusters. The campus goes live in phases from late 2027. CloudKey said it prefers designs using gallium nitride power stages for efficiency and is evaluating semiconductor suppliers with its manufacturing partners. CloudKey said demand from AI companies has pushed rack densities above 60 kW, and that standard power equipment is no longer efficient enough for the next generation of GPU clusters.
